sources.notes: Cartoon of Cecil Rhodes after he announced plans for a telegraph line and railway from Cape Town to Cairo; published in a British humor magazine.

sources.title: Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings (from the St. Petersburg album)
sources.author: Bichitr (Mughal court painter)

sources.alt: A richly decorated Mughal painting framed by borders of colored flowers and Persian calligraphy: a seated emperor with a gold halo and crescent behind him sits on a large hourglass-shaped throne and is handed a book by a white-bearded old man in brown robes; below the old man, two crowned or hatted foreigners and a young artist holding a small portrait look up, and winged cherub figures flank the hourglass.
sources.credit: Jahangir Preferring a Sufi Shaikh to Kings, Bichitr, c. 1615-1618. Freer Gallery of Art via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
sources.notes: Art historians identify the figures below the emperor as an Ottoman sultan and King James I of England, with Bichitr's self-portrait at the bottom; the winged figures reflect European art that reached the Mughal court.

sources.title: En Chine: Le gateau des Rois et... des Empereurs (China, the cake of kings and emperors)
sources.author: Henri Meyer (cartoonist), Le Petit Journal (Supplement illustre)
sources.repository: Wikimedia Commons (file page records the source institution and public-domain tag)
sources.call_number: Le Petit Journal, supplement of January 16, 1898, p. 24 (Cornell University Library, Persuasive Maps: PJ Mode Collection)
sources.rights: Wikimedia Commons file page: 'Public domain' (tags PD-old-auto-1923, PD-old-auto-expired); published in Paris in 1898.
sources.reuse: public domain (published 1898)
sources.modified: unmodified except Wikimedia Commons' scaled JPEG rendering of the file (upload.wikimedia.org thumbnail; 960 px wide for tall images, 1280 px wide for wide images)
sources.alt: A color French cartoon: around a round cake labeled 'CHINE' with slices marked 'KIAO-TCHEOU' and 'PORT-ARTHUR', five figures with knives crowd the table (an elderly queen with a crown, a man in a spiked German helmet, a man in a Russian cap, a young woman in a red-white-blue cap, and a man in Japanese dress), while a caricatured Chinese official in the back raises both hands in alarm; the caption reads 'En Chine, Le gateau des Rois et... des Empereurs'.
sources.credit: En Chine: Le gateau des Rois et... des Empereurs, Henri Meyer, Le Petit Journal, Jan. 16, 1898. Wikimedia Commons (public domain).
sources.notes: The figures are generally read as Britain (Queen Victoria), Germany (Wilhelm II), Russia (Nicholas II), France (Marianne) and Japan; the Chinese official is drawn as a caricature, which reflects the French view of the time.
